critical_code_review_comments: CRITICAL BUG FIXED: The main agent's refactoring introduced a JavaScript hoisting bug - useEffect was placed BEFORE the useCallback definitions it referenced. In JavaScript, const/let declarations are NOT hoisted like function declarations, so referencing them before definition causes a ReferenceError.
The fix was simple: move useCallback definitions BEFORE the useEffect that uses them in the dependency array.
DOMPurify sanitization is correctly implemented in CustomerDetailPage.js and LeadsPage.js
AuthContext useMemo/useCallback refactoring is working correctly
All console.log/error/warn statements have been removed from application code

rca_of_the_issue.root_cause: JavaScript hoisting behavior - const/let declarations are NOT hoisted. The main agent placed useEffect (which referenced fetchDashboardData in its dependency array) BEFORE the useCallback definition of fetchDashboardData. This caused a ReferenceError: Cannot access 'fetchDashboardData' before initialization.
reproduction_steps: 3. Observe runtime error: 'Cannot access fetchDashboardData before initialization'
rca_of_the_issue.mitigation: Always define useCallback/useMemo hooks BEFORE any useEffect that references them in its dependency array. This is a common React pattern that must be followed.
